LUMTAIL-FORMATS(7) Miscellaneous Information Manual LUMTAIL-FORMATS(7)

NAME

lumtail-formats — recognized log formats, normalized fields and severity mappings

DESCRIPTION

Read this page to choose a parser, find field names for filters and interpret the severity printed by lumtail(1). For a first inspection, export a few complete records:

lumtail --output json --limit 5 application.log
lumtail --list-modules

The JSON fields object shows the keys available to filters and templates. Values are strings, including numeric and Boolean values; nested objects and arrays are compact JSON strings. The top-level raw, file and line properties identify original record content and its source location.

PARSER SELECTION

Modules are tried separately for each record, in descending priority. The first complete match wins. Equal priorities keep registration order, with built-ins before custom modules. Built-ins are:

Module Priority Input
json 80 JSON Lines and supported JSON profiles
cef 78 Common Event Format 0 and 1
leef 77 Log Event Extended Format 1.0 and 2.0
fail2ban 75 Native Fail2ban text
syslog 70 RFC 3164, RFC 5424 and rsyslog timestamps
web-error 65 Apache and Nginx file error logs
access 60 Common and Combined access logs
auditd.raw -1000 Standalone Linux Audit RAW records
plain -1000 Fallback for unrecognized input

Custom rules default to priority 100 and are described in lumtail-rules(5). To force a parser:

lumtail --module json application.log

Forced parsing still sends unmatched records to plain. An unknown module name returns status 2. Suricata, Zeek and Kubernetes records are JSON profiles; select them with ‘--module json’.

JSON LINES

The json module accepts one JSON object per physical header line. Top-level keys remain available; duplicate keys use the last value. Large integer digits, including values beyond 64 bits, are preserved. JSON nesting is limited to 64 levels.

Generic aliases use the first supplied key in these lists:

timestamp
timestamp, time, ts, @timestamp
level
level, severity, log_level
source
source, logger, service, app, component
message
message, msg, log

Without a message alias, the original input becomes the message. Severity uses the case-insensitive aliases in lumtail(1), including numeric Pino/Bunyan levels 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60. JSON records also receive the following producer projections when their required shapes and types match.

Suricata EVE alerts

The record must have exact ‘event_type="alert"’ and an object-valued alert. Its format stays json.

alert.severity
Integer 1 maps to CRITICAL, 2 to ERROR and 3 to WARN, overriding generic severity. Other nonnegative 64-bit integers remain in alert_severity and original_level with UNKNOWN severity.
alert.signature
Supplies signature and a fallback message.
alert.signature_id
A nonnegative 64-bit integer supplies signature_id.
alert.category, alert.action
String values supply category and action.
dest_ip, dest_port
Literal IPv4/IPv6 and integer port 0 through 65535 supply dst_ip and dst_port.

The native payload and top-level EVE fields stay available. Valid nested aliases replace conflicting derived top-level aliases. An explicit generic message/source takes precedence over the signature message and default source ‘suricata’, including an explicit empty string.

Suricata EVE observations

Object payloads for exact event types http, dns, tls, fileinfo, anomaly and flow receive these additional aliases:

http
http_hostname, http_url, http_method, http_protocol, http_status, http_length, http_content_type, http_user_agent.
dns
dns_type, dns_id, dns_version, dns_rrname, dns_rrtype, dns_rcode, dns_queries, dns_answers, dns_grouped.
tls
tls_sni, tls_version, tls_subject, tls_issuerdn, tls_fingerprint, tls_serial, tls_notbefore, tls_notafter, tls_ja3, tls_ja3s, tls_ja4.
fileinfo
file_name, file_size, file_state, file_md5, file_sha1, file_sha256, file_stored.
anomaly
anomaly_type, anomaly_event, anomaly_layer, anomaly_app_proto.
flow
flow_state, flow_reason, flow_start, flow_end, flow_age, flow_pkts_toserver, flow_pkts_toclient, flow_bytes_toserver, flow_bytes_toclient, flow_alerted.

Text requires strings, counters require nonnegative integer JSON values and stored/alerted flags require Booleans. HTTP status accepts a three-digit integer or string from 100 through 599. DNS supports v3 and legacy v2/unversioned scalar shapes. For v3, scalar query aliases require exactly one object in queries; arrays and the complete payload stay available.

Validated destination endpoints supply dst_ip and dst_port; string-valued proto supplies protocol. Generic severity is kept for these observations.
